idiom_name: Consumer({'group.id': ...}) + commit(msg) inside the poll loop
implementation_notes: Default Python realization where the log is the broker: group.id names the durable subscription and the committed offset is the retained position, bounded by the topic's retention. Choose it when Python consumers share a Kafka cluster with other services and replay is routine.
code_sketch:
from confluent_kafka import Consumer
c = Consumer({"group.id": "billing-ledger",
              "enable.auto.commit": False,
              "auto.offset.reset": "earliest"})
c.subscribe(["orders"])
while True:
    for msg in c.consume(100, timeout=1.0):   # bounded catch-up batch
        handle(msg.value())                   # idempotent
        c.commit(msg)                         # checkpoint after the side effect
pitfalls: Committing a message you have not finished is the classic loss bug; committing the whole batch late replays everything after a crash.
A rebalance between poll and commit can replay the last batch, so handlers must be idempotent.

variants.name: MQTT persistent session with paho-mqtt
variants.implementation_notes: Where MQTT is the transport, the broker holds the session and queues QoS 1/2 publications for the offline client id. Choose it for IoT-style consumers; note the split responsibility - the broker keeps the subscription, the client must keep the same id and its own acknowledgement handling idempotent.
variants.code_sketch:
client = mqtt.Client(client_id="billing-ledger", clean_session=False)
client.on_connect = lambda c, u, f, rc, props: c.subscribe("orders/#", qos=1)
client.connect(broker)
client.loop_forever()   # broker queued messages while this client was offline
pitfalls: paho-mqtt keeps the client session in memory only, so a restart loses in-flight QoS 2 state even with clean_session=False.
Using a fresh or random client id per run discards the broker-held session and its queued backlog.
